diagnostics.title: alias unavailable
diagnostics.summary: the selected worktree is not ready to serve this alias. start its entry service and check tnl status.
diagnostics.description: the alias selection or its selected app run changed before this request could be admitted.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the selected alias service is unavailable
causes: the selected service stopped or is reprovisioning
the alias is handing off to another worktree

publisher: start the entry service in the selected worktree and check tnl status
visitor: retry after the alias is ready

diagnostics.title: alias name is too deeply nested
diagnostics.summary: this hostname uses more labels beneath your namespace than the server allows on its managed domain. use a shorter name.
diagnostics.description: the server limits the depth of member public URLs on its managed deployment domain; this restriction does not apply to custom domains.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the name exceeds this domain's depth limit
causes: the alias name contains more DNS labels than this server permits beneath a member namespace

publisher: use fewer labels beneath your namespace

diagnostics.title: webhook receiver unavailable
diagnostics.summary: this webhook has no matching ready receiver. start the declared service in a worktree with the same endpoint policy.
diagnostics.description: tnl could not select a current local service for the declared webhook endpoint.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the webhook has no ready local receiver
causes: the declared service is stopped, starting, or no longer has a live tunnel
worktrees use conflicting endpoint policies

publisher: start the configured service and check webhook readiness
use matching path, method, and source-policy declarations across worktrees

diagnostics.title: webhook delivery failed
diagnostics.summary: a selected webhook receiver failed or timed out. check the worktree's handler before requesting provider redelivery.
diagnostics.description: tnl could not obtain successful acknowledgments from every selected webhook receiver.
diagnostics.diagram_label: a webhook receiver did not succeed
causes: a selected local service returned a non-2xx response or stopped
a receiver timed out or returned a conflicting verification response

publisher: check each selected worktree's webhook handler and signature verification
handle duplicate event IDs because provider retries can revisit successful receivers

diagnostics.title: oauth callback unavailable
diagnostics.summary: the stable OAuth callback is not ready. keep an app tunnel running and retry sign-in shortly.
diagnostics.description: the local callback publisher or its state could not accept this login attempt.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the stable OAuth callback is unavailable
causes: the callback public URL is still provisioning or changing its publisher
local callback state is unavailable or full

visitor: start sign-in again after the callback publisher is ready
publisher: keep the registered app or tnl publish running and check callback readiness
retry sign-in after the publisher recovers

diagnostics.title: oauth callback expired
diagnostics.summary: this login callback expired, was already used, or belongs to a stopped tunnel. start sign-in again in the intended worktree.
diagnostics.description: tnl could not find a current, unused local callback mapping for this OAuth response.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the OAuth callback no longer has a current tunnel
causes: the login attempt expired or its state was already consumed
the originating tunnel stopped or its publish run was replaced

visitor: open the intended worktree and start a new sign-in
publisher: keep the originating app tunnel running while signing in

diagnostics.title: target unavailable
diagnostics.summary: tnl could not reach the target or get a usable response from it. check that the target is running, then try again.
diagnostics.description: tnl could not reach the target at startup or while serving a visitor request.
diagnostics.diagram_label: tnl cannot reach the target
causes: the target stopped or has not finished starting
the target hostname or port cannot be reached from the machine running tnl
the HTTPS target's certificate is not trusted or does not match its hostname
the target closed the connection or returned an invalid HTTP response

cases.action: start the target and check its listening port

cases.description: the target did not respond before the connection timed out.
cases.action: check whether the target is running and accepting requests

visitor: ask the public URL owner to check the target, then retry
publisher: check the target passed to `tnl publish` or registered by the app integration
verify that the target accepts connections from the machine running `tnl` and that its HTTPS certificate is trusted
if the command failed at startup, rerun it; if the tunnel is still running, retry the visit after restarting the target

diagnostics.title: invalid target
diagnostics.summary: tnl could not use the configured target.
diagnostics.description: tnl rejected the target before contacting it.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the target configuration is invalid
causes: the target port is missing or outside the valid range
the target contains a path, query, fragment, credentials, or whitespace
the target is not an HTTP or HTTPS origin with a valid DNS name or IP address

publisher: use a bare port such as `3000`, `localhost:3000`, or an HTTP or HTTPS origin
run the command again with the corrected target

diagnostics.title: invalid public url
diagnostics.summary: tnl could not use the hostname assigned to the public url.
diagnostics.description: the tnl server assigned a malformed or noncanonical public url hostname.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the server returned an invalid hostname
causes: the server returned a malformed hostname
the client and server use incompatible public url contracts

publisher: verify that tnl is connected to the intended server
check control API and `tnld` logs on a self-hosted server

diagnostics.title: request rejected
diagnostics.summary: tnl rejected the request before contacting the local service. use the exact public url with an ordinary HTTPS request.
diagnostics.description: the request reached tnl but did not match the public url or supported HTTP request form.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the visitor request was rejected before the local service
causes: the request hostname and TLS server name do not match the public url
the request uses CONNECT or an absolute URL
the request contains too many header fields

visitor: use the exact HTTPS url provided by the public URL owner
send an ordinary HTTP request rather than a forward-proxy request
publisher: check the requested hostname and any clients constructing unusual HTTP requests

diagnostics.title: request misdirected
diagnostics.summary: this HTTP/2 connection belongs to another public url. retry on a new connection to the requested hostname.
diagnostics.description: the browser reused an HTTP/2 connection for a different public url under the same certificate. tnl asked it to retry on a new connection.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the visitor request reached the wrong public url
causes: the HTTP/2 request hostname differs from the TLS server name used for this connection

visitor: retry the exact HTTPS url on a new connection
publisher: check the requested hostname and any clients reusing HTTP/2 connections

diagnostics.title: request limit reached
diagnostics.summary: tnl has reached the concurrent request limit for this public url. wait briefly, then retry.
diagnostics.description: too many requests are active at once; tnl did not contact the local service for this request.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the request limit stopped this request before the local service
causes: the public url has reached its concurrent request limit, including streams and upgrades

cases.description: all concurrent request slots were in use when this visitor arrived.
cases.action: wait for active requests to finish, then retry

publisher: check `--request-limit` and local service concurrency if saturation persists

diagnostics.title: ip address not allowed
diagnostics.summary: this public url does not allow connections from your IP address.
diagnostics.description: the public url's IP policy blocked this connection before any request reached the local service.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the IP policy denied this visitor before the local service
causes: the visitor's current public IP address is outside the public url's allowed addresses
IP addresses can change when a visitor changes networks or uses a VPN

visitor: ask the public URL owner to allow your current IP address
publisher: check `--allow-ip` and the public url's IP policy
only use `--allow-all-ips` if the local service should be available to everyone

diagnostics.title: dev command loops
diagnostics.summary: tnl dev started itself instead of the local service. set dev.command to start your app directly.
diagnostics.description: the configured development command led back to tnl dev, so the local service never started.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the development command loops before starting the local service
causes: `dev.command` calls `tnl dev` directly
`dev.command` runs the package.json `dev` script, and that script starts `tnl dev`

publisher: set `dev.command` to the app command, such as `["next", "dev"]` for Next.js or `["vite"]` for Vite
for another app, run its binary directly or use a separate script such as `dev:app`; `scripts.dev` may then run `tnl dev`
run `tnl init` to review the project setup, then start your app again

diagnostics.title: framework registration timed out
diagnostics.summary: tnl dev did not receive the framework's target registration before the startup timeout.
diagnostics.description: the development service did not register a listening target with tnl dev in time.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the framework did not register its target
causes: the Next.js or Vite integration is missing from the active config
a Node or Bun service did not call `tnl.register(server)`
framework startup exceeded the configured timeout

publisher: run `tnl init` and complete the reported framework setup
check the active framework config or call `tnl.register(server)` for Node or Bun
use `--port` when there is no integration, or increase `dev.startupTimeout` if startup needs more time

diagnostics.title: target mismatch
diagnostics.summary: the development service listened on a different target than the port required by tnl dev.
diagnostics.description: the framework reported a different listening port from the one tnl dev required.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the registered target does not match the required port
causes: the framework ignored or overrode the requested port
the port was occupied and the framework switched to another one

publisher: remove competing port settings from the project script
when using `--port`, free that port and keep the framework on the exact value

diagnostics.title: authentication timed out
diagnostics.summary: interactive authentication did not finish before login expired. run the command again and complete sign-in promptly.
diagnostics.description: interactive authentication expired before tnl received a login.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the interactive login expired
causes: sign-in did not finish before the interactive limit
the provider's device code expired sooner

publisher: run the command again for a new login URL and code
finish sign-in before the new login expires

diagnostics.title: authentication required
diagnostics.summary: tnl could not authenticate this request. log in again or check the supplied access token.
diagnostics.description: the control API or authority API did not accept the current credential.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the server rejected authentication
causes: the saved session expired or was revoked
the supplied access token is invalid

publisher: run `tnl auth login` explicitly, then retry
if using `--access-token`, check that the token belongs to the selected server

diagnostics.title: server unavailable
diagnostics.summary: tnl could not reach the control API or authority API. check the server address and try again.
diagnostics.description: the selected server is unavailable or did not respond in time.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the server did not respond
causes: a network connection or the server is temporarily unavailable
the selected control URL points to the wrong server

publisher: verify `--server` or `TNL_SERVER` and network connectivity
retry with backoff; if self-hosted, check control and authority health

diagnostics.title: rate limited
diagnostics.summary: the server is limiting requests. wait before retrying.
diagnostics.description: the control API or authority API limited this request rate.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the server limited the request rate
causes: the server received too many requests in a short period

publisher: wait for the server's Retry-After interval before retrying
reduce the rate of automated requests if the limit persists

diagnostics.title: dns setup pending
diagnostics.summary: the domain's DNS setup is not ready. check its records, then retry after they propagate.
diagnostics.description: the server is waiting for DNS authority or hostname setup.
diagnostics.diagram_label: DNS setup has not completed
causes: required DNS records have not propagated or are incorrect

publisher: check the requested DNS records with your domain provider
retry when the domain becomes ready

diagnostics.title: service selection ambiguous
diagnostics.summary: the project configures multiple services. select one by name and run the command again.
diagnostics.description: tnl cannot choose one project service when several are configured.
diagnostics.diagram_label: multiple project services matched and none was selected
causes: `tnl publish` was run without a service name, or an app directory matches multiple configured services

publisher: choose one of the sorted service names printed by tnl
pass the service name to the integration or run `tnl publish <service>`

diagnostics.title: public url conflict
diagnostics.summary: tnl could not create or reconcile the public url because its hostname, identity, or lifecycle conflicts with the requested public url.
diagnostics.description: the requested public url conflicts with an existing hostname, identity, or lifecycle state.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the control API rejected the requested public url
causes: the hostname is owned by another public url, team, or membership
an existing public url has a different identity or is suspended, deleted, or in use

publisher: check `tnl team current` and `tnl url list`
choose a hostname the selected team owns or resolve the existing public url's lifecycle conflict

diagnostics.title: provisioning stalled
diagnostics.summary: public url provisioning has not completed. tnl is still retrying certificate or publisher connection work.
diagnostics.description: the public url is not yet routable; tnl is still retrying certificate or publisher connection work.
diagnostics.diagram_label: the public url is not yet routable
causes: certificate authorization or issuance is pending
one or more assigned relay services are unavailable

cases.description: certificate work is still pending for this publish run.
cases.action: keep tnl running and check certificate issuance on a self-hosted server

cases.description: an assigned relay is not ready for this publish run.
cases.action: keep tnl running and check relay health on a self-hosted server

publisher: keep the command running while tnl retries
check `tnl status` and, on a self-hosted server, control and relay health
